assign.request: Cheap, never-stale page references. Owner: loading a whole page (or a big page.jsonl) just to get its icon and title is too much; a hand-run cache goes stale; DRY. Today ext/Mention/maps/refs.js is generated by a script someone must re-run (sync.mjs). Make the index rebuild itself: when a page.js's icon/title or a page.jsonl's first line changes, the dev server (it already watches) updates the one index; page.jsonl pages included. Title renames then show everywhere. One index, computed, never typed. Write the decision + the alternative the owner floated (a per-folder meta.json snapshot) in one line on your card.
steps: read sync.mjs, refs.js, watch.js, Directory.js precedent
extract a shared icon-sync function sync.mjs and the watcher both call
build Server/plugins/MentionSync.js on the shared watcher, debounced like Directory.js
prove it: rename a page.js icon live, show refs.js update with no manual script run
update ext/Mention docs (readme + doc/syntax.md) and write the decision
create board card with the one-line decision

assign.now: proved it live: flipped Sidebar's icon, watched refs.js update, reverted

decision.question: how should ext/Mention/maps/refs.js stay fresh without a human re-running sync.mjs?
options: computed-on-change index on the dev server's one shared fs.watch handle (same shape as Directory.js/directory.json)
a per-folder meta.json snapshot (the owner's own alternative)
decision.why: one index, one shape, computed — the snapshot is a second index format next to refs.js (Law 6), and every reader (including the sibling ref-content-row feature) would need to know which of two places to check for a page's icon.

log.msg: pass 1 (icon, text-only, cheap) extracted from sync.mjs into sync-icon.mjs, shared by sync.mjs and the new Server/plugins/MentionSync.js watcher. class_card (pass 2) stays manual/sync.mjs-only — needs a real headless page load, too expensive per keystroke, and Mention.js's own live() already covers the hot case. page.jsonl pages generalised in resolve_icon() (borrows the icon of the jsonl page's own 'class' template) even though no current refs.js entry is backed by one.

proof: restarted the monorepo dev server (picks up the new plugin), held live-reload for core/Sidebar + ext/Mention, flipped Sidebar page.js's icon to a test value — server log: '[MentionSync] refs.js icon auto-synced (1 changed): /framework/core/Sidebar/ -> view_sidebar_test_123' within ~2s, no sync.mjs run. Reverted the icon, refs.js synced back the same way. Ran sync.mjs standalone afterward: 0 changes (already current) — manual and auto paths agree.
task-loop chase 1 of 2: left to heartbeat

assign.title: ext/Mention: refs.js auto-syncs its icon, no sync.mjs run needed
assign.outcome:
**Landed: `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js`'s icon rebuilds itself.** [`Server/plugins/MentionSync.js`](/framework/servex/fs/?file=Server) sits on the dev server's one shared `fs.watch` handle (same shape as `Directory.js`/`directory.json`) and, on any real change to a watched `page.js` or `page.jsonl`, debounces then re-derives that entry's icon via the shared [`sync-icon.mjs`](/framework/servex/fs/?file=Server) (extracted from `sync.mjs`'s own pass 1 — one computation, not two) and rewrites `refs.js` only if it actually changed.

- [x] rebuilds on a page.js icon change, no manual script — proved live: flipped `core/Sidebar/page.js`'s icon, server logged `[MentionSync] refs.js icon auto-synced` within ~2s, `refs.js` updated; reverted, synced back (`task.jsonl`, 13:30-13:32).
- [x] page.jsonl pages included — `resolve_icon()` borrows a jsonl page's own template (`class` on its first line) for its icon; no current curated entry is backed by one, so this is proven by code path, not yet by a live example.
- [x] decision + the owner's own alternative written down (one line on the card too): a computed-on-change index on the shared watcher, not a per-folder `meta.json` snapshot — a snapshot is a second index shape next to `refs.js` (Law 6).
- [ ] not automated, by design: `class_card` still needs a human `sync.mjs` run (headless page load, too expensive per keystroke) — `Mention.js`'s own `live()` already covers the common case.

Docs: [`ext/Mention/readme.md`](/framework/ext/Mention/) watch-out bullet rewritten; [`doc/syntax.md`](/framework/ext/Mention/md/doc/syntax/) gets a new section with the decision and the page.jsonl generalisation; `Server/readme.md` and `Server/doc/watch.md` note the new BOOT_TEST-honouring plugin. Review: `node Server/review.mjs --status` → reviewed: pass (mastermind's own read, no page/layout touched).
